newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks seen likely to fall, then recover.
newsitem.headline: China stocks seen likely to fall, then recover.

text.p: China's share markets are likely to see a sharp reaction from investors to mark the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, but many people will be waiting eagerly to buy into any significant falls, brokers said on Thursday.
John Crossman, Shanghai representative for Jardine Fleming, predicted the China B share market could be down five percent or more initially but could end the day up as much as two percent.
"I think we'll see a sharp reaction down from locals, but there are foreigners who have been waiting for this buying opportunity for quite a while," he said.
"I think money's going to go into the market, so there's a very good chance of down in the morning and up in the afternoon," he added.
A Chinese broker said he expected a sharp fall on very small volume initially but said there was a strong possibility of a quick rebound.
